searchText: Yes, that was the idea with the change, basically I meant based on geth, like `evm t8n` which is "statetransition", we could have `evm blockprogression` or something to seal blocks according to certain rules. Given a parent header, etc, spits out the next header And chain reorganization? If it would use the logic from clients core that what I intended to have in the first place. If you would need to re implement the whole logic yourself from scratch then no need I don't see what chain reorg has to do with anything? Block progressions is: "Given parent `P`, give me a child `C` which has these fields `[ timestamp, stateroot, txRoot ...]`" So if you want to manufacture a reorg,then you do "child1 = BlockProgression(P, ..); child2 = BlockProgression(P, ...); child3 = BlockProgression( child1, ...), ... " and build up the chain blocks you want But yes, I mean the core logic of doing that is fairly small, and once you've implemented it in retesteth it shouldn't change a lot
